title: Pony's Arena Allocator - Pony
excerpt: Here’s how it was. We’d been running stress tests on the TCP system in ponyc every day for a really long time. Those tests hadn’t failed in forever. There’s two ways you can look at “no tests are failing.” Either your system is rock solid or your tests aren’t covering enough of the codebase. I’d long felt that the lack of stress test failures was the result of “tests aren’t good enough.”
content_html:
Here’s how it was. We’d been running stress tests on the TCP system in ponyc every day for a really long time. Those tests hadn’t failed in forever. There’s two ways you can look at “no tests are failing.” Either your system is rock solid or your tests aren’t covering enough of the codebase. I’d long felt that the lack of stress test failures was the result of “tests aren’t good enough.”

A few months back, I did something about that. I took the TCP stress tests that did the same thing on every run and added some “swarm testing goodness” — randomizing what they were doing and how they were being run, from run to run. A lot more code was getting exercised, and out popped a bunch of bugs.

This post is about one of those “bugs.”

Under certain usage patterns, memory grew without bound. A little investigation showed that it wasn’t a bug in the TCP code itself. The test was triggering an interesting collection of edge cases in the Pony runtime’s allocator.

There were three reasons the old allocator could hold on to memory in a way that could lead to the degenerate case I was seeing with the failing stress test instance.

  1. In Pony, a message is allocated by its sender and freed by its receiver. About half of all frees land on a different thread than the one that did the allocation. A large block freed on the wrong thread stayed reserved, never reclaimed. A workload that passed blocks between threads reserved fresh address space for every block it allocated and freed, without bound. At ten thousand blocks, it was still climbing, about 4.3 MiB of address space per block.

  2. Once memory was carved into 32-byte slots, it held 32-byte objects forever. The allocator never returned it for a different size.

  3. Two adjacent free blocks were never merged. The old allocator kept a sorted free list, and mixed-size workloads slowed to a crawl walking it. 0.49 seconds to allocate at 4,000 blocks. 39.6 seconds at 16,000. 64,000 blocks did not finish in nine minutes.

All three came from the same place: the old allocator used a global pool with per-size-class free lists shared by every thread. No thread tracked which memory it allocated.

The fix for all three: make each thread track the memory it allocates — what’s in use, what’s free, when a region is empty. That tracking is what the old allocator lacked. With it, the allocator can merge freed memory, return empty regions to the OS, and reuse memory across threads.

The New Allocator¶

I built a new allocator, inspired by snmalloc’s region-based design. Memory is organized in two tiers: large regions requested from the OS, split into smaller arenas. Each arena belongs to one thread. That thread is responsible for all the bookkeeping in its arenas — tracking what’s allocated, what’s free, and when memory can go back to the OS. Cross-thread frees are batched and routed to the owning thread rather than handled globally.

Regions and arenas¶

The allocator requests memory from the OS in large aligned chunks called regions — 256 MiB on 64-bit machines, 64 MiB on 32-bit. Regions are shared by every thread and never unmapped. By not unmapping regions, a thread walking the region list has a memory safety guarantee that the rest of the design depends on.

Threads take arenas from regions. An arena is 8 MiB on 64-bit, 2 MiB on 32-bit, and each is bound to a thread. The owning thread is responsible for maintaining the arena’s bookkeeping. When an arena empties, its physical pages go back to the OS, but its address space stays parked in the region for reuse.

Freeing memory starts with finding which arena it belongs to. An arena’s starting address is aligned to its own size. On 64-bit, every arena starts on an 8 MiB boundary. Mask the low bits of any pointer and you get the arena’s base address. One instruction. No memory read. Nice and fast. We like nice and fast over here in Ponyland.

Units, slabs, and the bitmap¶

An arena is divided into 16 KiB units. A slab is one or more contiguous units serving one size class. There are 16 size classes, from 32 bytes up to 1 MiB, each a power of two. For small classes, multiple objects fit into a single unit — a 32-byte class fits 512 objects per unit. Large classes span multiple units.

Free or used is one bit per unit in a bitmap. An 8 MiB arena has 512 units, which fits in 8 bitmap words on a 64-bit machine.

Two free units next to each other in memory are two zero bits next to each other in the bitmap. They’re already one contiguous span; there’s nothing to merge. Finding N free units is scanning for N consecutive zeros. No merge code. No sorted free list. No O(n) walk. The old allocator’s block boundary — where two adjacent free blocks never merged — can’t happen here because the representation doesn’t allow it. Adjacency in memory is adjacency in the bitmap, and adjacency in the bitmap is a span. Always was.

Ascending first-fit in one direction leaves long runs in the other. Without that split, single-unit allocations would fragment the large spans that multi-unit slabs need.

Arena bookkeeping — the bitmap, per-unit records — lives at the arena’s start. Nothing sits in front of an allocated object.

Cross-thread frees¶

In Pony, a message is allocated by the thread running the sender and freed by the thread running the receiver. Those are usually different threads. Cross-thread frees aren’t an edge case — they happen constantly, and the allocator has to be fast at them.

The direct approach is one atomic operation per foreign free: push the freed object onto the owning thread’s inbox. However, testing showed that under contention performance collapsed. The direct approach doesn’t work.

Instead, the freeing thread collects freed objects and sends them to the owner in batches. One atomic for 32 frees instead of 32 atomics for 32 frees. The performance difference between the batched and unbatched is huge. The owning thread processes the freed memory and can reuse it.

The thread cache¶

Batching cross-thread frees is faster than one atomic per free, but sending the batch back to the owner still costs something. Better to avoid sending it at all when you can. Each thread keeps a small cache of recently freed blocks, one per size class. When a thread frees a block that belongs to another thread, it goes into the local cache. If the thread later needs a block of that size, it reuses the cached one directly — no cross-thread coordination, no batch to send. The block only gets routed back to its owner when the cache overflows, the thread goes idle, or the thread exits.

Each size class gets a cache depth: the byte budget (256 KiB) divided by the class size or the profile’s floor count, whichever is larger, capped at 512 blocks. Large classes need the floor — without it, the byte budget divides down to zero or one entry, and every churn cycle pays a full slab reserve and release.

The idle return flushes the entire cache, so the floor costs resident memory only while a thread actively churns. Once a thread parks, its cache is empty.

Memory return¶

When a thread has been idle long enough, it starts giving memory back to the OS. The old allocator never did this. A thread that goes briefly idle and gets work again keeps its memory. But a thread that stays idle gives back everything it holds. Cache, dirty pages, all of it. A parked thread holds nothing.

The mechanism is a timed tick. An idle thread checks in every 10 milliseconds, doubling the interval each quiet visit up to a 500-millisecond cap. Once it reaches the cap, all held memory goes back to the OS.

While a thread is active, small freed slabs stay resident and get returned in batches rather than one at a time. Larger freed slabs get returned immediately.

I started this post talking about the old allocator hanging on to memory in problematic ways, so what does it look like now? Here are some numbers from testing: 105 MiB of size-class memory, thread goes idle, resident memory falls to 6.5 MiB. The old allocator held all of it, 104 MiB. At a 1 GiB working set, the arena peaks at 1,025 MiB and settles to 27 MiB after idle. The old allocator: 1,019 MiB, start to finish.

The tuning knob¶

Not every program has the same needs. I spent several days testing different tunable parameters that let you trade memory usage for performance. They’re exposed in a new flag, --ponymemoryprofile, a scale from 1 to 10. The default is 3. At 1, the allocator returns memory to the OS as aggressively as possible — lowest footprint. At 10, it holds on to memory longer to avoid the cost of returning and re-acquiring it — highest throughput.

Every setting returns everything when a thread goes idle. The tradeoff only matters while a thread is actively working.

What’s next¶

The arena allocator is merged to main and is the default on every platform Pony supports. There’s one tradeoff worth knowing: the old allocator was faster in workloads where the working set exceeds the thread cache, because it never gave memory back. That’s the price of reclaiming.

I’m letting the stress tests run for several days to see if they shake out any bugs. Expect a release by the end of the month.

Cross-thread frees are batched and routed to the owning thread rather than handled globally.

sentences.en: I built a new allocator, inspired by snmalloc’s region-based design.
sentences.zh: 受到 snmalloc 基于区域的设计的启发，我构建了一个新的分配器。

sentences.en: Memory is organized in two tiers: large regions requested from the OS, split into smaller arenas.
sentences.zh: 内存分为两层：操作系统请求的大区域，分为更小的区域。

sentences.en: Each arena belongs to one thread.
sentences.zh: 每个竞技场属于一个线程。

sentences.en: That thread is responsible for all the bookkeeping in its arenas — tracking what’s allocated, what’s free, and when memory can go back to the OS.
sentences.zh: 该线程负责其领域中的所有簿记工作 - 跟踪已分配的内容、空闲的内容以及内存何时可以返回操作系统。

sentences.en: Cross-thread frees are batched and routed to the owning thread rather than handled globally.
sentences.zh: 跨线程释放被批量并路由到所属线程，而不是全局处理。

blocks.html_en: Regions and arenas¶

sentences.en: Regions and arenas¶
sentences.zh: 地区和竞技场¶

blocks.html_en: The allocator requests memory from the OS in large aligned chunks called regions — 256 MiB on 64-bit machines, 64 MiB on 32-bit. Regions are shared by every thread and never unmapped. By not unmapping regions, a thread walking the region list has a memory safety guarantee that the rest of the design depends on.

sentences.en: The allocator requests memory from the OS in large aligned chunks called regions — 256 MiB on 64-bit machines, 64 MiB on 32-bit.
sentences.zh: 分配器以称为区域的大对齐块从操作系统请求内存 - 64 位计算机上为 256 MiB，32 位计算机上为 64 MiB。

sentences.en: Regions are shared by every thread and never unmapped.
sentences.zh: 区域由每个线程共享，并且永远不会取消映射。

sentences.en: By not unmapping regions, a thread walking the region list has a memory safety guarantee that the rest of the design depends on.
sentences.zh: 通过不取消映射区域，遍历区域列表的线程具有其余设计所依赖的内存安全保证。

blocks.html_en: Threads take arenas from regions. An arena is 8 MiB on 64-bit, 2 MiB on 32-bit, and each is bound to a thread. The owning thread is responsible for maintaining the arena’s bookkeeping. When an arena empties, its physical pages go back to the OS, but its address space stays parked in the region for reuse.

sentences.en: Threads take arenas from regions.
sentences.zh: 线程从区域获取竞技场。

sentences.en: An arena is 8 MiB on 64-bit, 2 MiB on 32-bit, and each is bound to a thread.
sentences.zh: 一个 arena 在 64 位上为 8 MiB，在 32 位上为 2 MiB，并且每个都绑定到一个线程。

sentences.en: The owning thread is responsible for maintaining the arena’s bookkeeping.
sentences.zh: 拥有线程负责维护竞技场的簿记。

sentences.en: When an arena empties, its physical pages go back to the OS, but its address space stays parked in the region for reuse.
sentences.zh: 当竞技场清空时，其物理页面将返回操作系统，但其地址空间仍保留在该区域中以供重用。

blocks.html_en: Freeing memory starts with finding which arena it belongs to. An arena’s starting address is aligned to its own size. On 64-bit, every arena starts on an 8 MiB boundary. Mask the low bits of any pointer and you get the arena’s base address. One instruction. No memory read. Nice and fast. We like nice and fast over here in Ponyland.

sentences.en: Freeing memory starts with finding which arena it belongs to.
sentences.zh: 释放内存首先要找到它属于哪个区域。

sentences.en: An arena’s starting address is aligned to its own size.
sentences.zh: 竞技场的起始地址与其自身的大小对齐。

sentences.en: On 64-bit, every arena starts on an 8 MiB boundary.
sentences.zh: 在 64 位上，每个 arena 都从 8 MiB 边界开始。

sentences.en: Mask the low bits of any pointer and you get the arena’s base address.
sentences.zh: 屏蔽任何指针的低位，您就可以获得竞技场的基地址。

sentences.en: One instruction.
sentences.zh: 一条指令。

sentences.en: No memory read.
sentences.zh: 没有读取内存。

sentences.en: Nice and fast.
sentences.zh: 又好又快。

sentences.en: We like nice and fast over here in Ponyland.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢 Ponyland 的这里又好又快。

blocks.html_en: Units, slabs, and the bitmap¶

sentences.en: Units, slabs, and the bitmap¶
sentences.zh: 单位、板和位图¶

blocks.html_en: An arena is divided into 16 KiB units. A slab is one or more contiguous units serving one size class. There are 16 size classes, from 32 bytes up to 1 MiB, each a power of two. For small classes, multiple objects fit into a single unit — a 32-byte class fits 512 objects per unit. Large classes span multiple units.

sentences.en: An arena is divided into 16 KiB units.
sentences.zh: 一个竞技场分为 16 KiB 单元。

sentences.en: A slab is one or more contiguous units serving one size class.
sentences.zh: 一块板是服务于一种尺寸等级的一个或多个连续单元。

sentences.en: There are 16 size classes, from 32 bytes up to 1 MiB, each a power of two.
sentences.zh: 有 16 个大小类别，从 32 字节到 1 MiB，每个类别都是 2 的幂。

sentences.en: For small classes, multiple objects fit into a single unit — a 32-byte class fits 512 objects per unit.
sentences.zh: 对于小类，多个对象适合一个单元 - 32 字节的类每个单元适合 512 个对象。

sentences.en: Large classes span multiple units.
sentences.zh: 大班跨越多个单元。

blocks.html_en: Free or used is one bit per unit in a bitmap. An 8 MiB arena has 512 units, which fits in 8 bitmap words on a 64-bit machine.

sentences.en: Free or used is one bit per unit in a bitmap.
sentences.zh: 空闲或已用是位图中每个单元一位。

sentences.en: An 8 MiB arena has 512 units, which fits in 8 bitmap words on a 64-bit machine.
sentences.zh: 8 MiB 的 arena 有 512 个单元，适合 64 位机器上的 8 个位图字。

blocks.html_en: Two free units next to each other in memory are two zero bits next to each other in the bitmap. They’re already one contiguous span; there’s nothing to merge. Finding N free units is scanning for N consecutive zeros. No merge code. No sorted free list. No O(n) walk. The old allocator’s block boundary — where two adjacent free blocks never merged — can’t happen here because the representation doesn’t allow it. Adjacency in memory is adjacency in the bitmap, and adjacency in the bitmap is a span. Always was.

sentences.en: Two free units next to each other in memory are two zero bits next to each other in the bitmap.
sentences.zh: 内存中彼此相邻的两个空闲单元是位图中彼此相邻的两个零位。

sentences.en: They’re already one contiguous span; there’s nothing to merge.
sentences.zh: 它们已经是一个连续的跨度；没有什么可以合并的。

sentences.en: Finding N free units is scanning for N consecutive zeros.
sentences.zh: 寻找N个空闲单元就是扫描N个连续的零。

sentences.en: No merge code.
sentences.zh: 没有合并代码。

sentences.en: No sorted free list.
sentences.zh: 没有排序的空闲列表。

sentences.en: No O(n) walk.
sentences.zh: 没有 O(n) 步行。

sentences.en: The old allocator’s block boundary — where two adjacent free blocks never merged — can’t happen here because the representation doesn’t allow it.
sentences.zh: 旧分配器的块边界（两个相邻的空闲块从未合并）在这里不可能发生，因为表示不允许。

sentences.en: Adjacency in memory is adjacency in the bitmap, and adjacency in the bitmap is a span.
sentences.zh: 内存中的邻接是位图中的邻接，位图中的邻接是跨度。

sentences.en: Always was.
sentences.zh: 一直都是。

blocks.html_en: Ascending first-fit in one direction leaves long runs in the other. Without that split, single-unit allocations would fragment the large spans that multi-unit slabs need.

sentences.en: Ascending first-fit in one direction leaves long runs in the other.
sentences.zh: 在一个方向上提升首次适应会在另一个方向上留下长跑。

sentences.en: Without that split, single-unit allocations would fragment the large spans that multi-unit slabs need.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这种分割，单个单元分配将会分割多单元板所需的大跨度。

blocks.html_en: Arena bookkeeping — the bitmap, per-unit records — lives at the arena’s start. Nothing sits in front of an allocated object.

sentences.en: Arena bookkeeping — the bitmap, per-unit records — lives at the arena’s start.
sentences.zh: 竞技场簿记——位图、每单位记录——存在于竞技场的开始阶段。

sentences.en: Nothing sits in front of an allocated object.
sentences.zh: 分配的对象前面没有任何东西。

blocks.html_en: Cross-thread frees¶

sentences.en: Cross-thread frees¶
sentences.zh: 跨线程释放¶

blocks.html_en: In Pony, a message is allocated by the thread running the sender and freed by the thread running the receiver. Those are usually different threads. Cross-thread frees aren’t an edge case — they happen constantly, and the allocator has to be fast at them.

sentences.en: In Pony, a message is allocated by the thread running the sender and freed by the thread running the receiver.
sentences.zh: 在 Pony 中，消息由运行发送者的线程分配，并由运行接收者的线程释放。

sentences.en: Those are usually different threads.
sentences.zh: 这些通常是不同的线程。

sentences.en: Cross-thread frees aren’t an edge case — they happen constantly, and the allocator has to be fast at them.
sentences.zh: 跨线程释放并不是一种边缘情况——它们不断发生，并且分配器必须快速处理它们。

blocks.html_en: The direct approach is one atomic operation per foreign free: push the freed object onto the owning thread’s inbox. However, testing showed that under contention performance collapsed. The direct approach doesn’t work.

sentences.en: The direct approach is one atomic operation per foreign free: push the freed object onto the owning thread’s inbox.
sentences.zh: 直接的方法是每个外部释放一个原子操作：将释放的对象推送到所属线程的收件箱中。

sentences.en: However, testing showed that under contention performance collapsed.
sentences.zh: 然而，测试表明，在争用情况下，性能崩溃了。

sentences.en: The direct approach doesn’t work.
sentences.zh: 直接的方法行不通。

blocks.html_en: Instead, the freeing thread collects freed objects and sends them to the owner in batches. One atomic for 32 frees instead of 32 atomics for 32 frees. The performance difference between the batched and unbatched is huge. The owning thread processes the freed memory and can reuse it.

sentences.en: Instead, the freeing thread collects freed objects and sends them to the owner in batches.
sentences.zh: 相反，释放线程收集释放的对象并将它们批量发送给所有者。

sentences.en: One atomic for 32 frees instead of 32 atomics for 32 frees.
sentences.zh: 一个原子可进行 32 次释放，而不是 32 个原子可进行 32 次释放。

sentences.en: The performance difference between the batched and unbatched is huge.
sentences.zh: 批处理和非批处理之间的性能差异是巨大的。

sentences.en: The owning thread processes the freed memory and can reuse it.
sentences.zh: 拥有线程处理释放的内存并可以重用它。

blocks.html_en: The thread cache¶

sentences.en: The thread cache¶
sentences.zh: 线程缓存¶

blocks.html_en: Batching cross-thread frees is faster than one atomic per free, but sending the batch back to the owner still costs something. Better to avoid sending it at all when you can. Each thread keeps a small cache of recently freed blocks, one per size class. When a thread frees a block that belongs to another thread, it goes into the local cache. If the thread later needs a block of that size, it reuses the cached one directly — no cross-thread coordination, no batch to send. The block only gets routed back to its owner when the cache overflows, the thread goes idle, or the thread exits.

sentences.en: Batching cross-thread frees is faster than one atomic per free, but sending the batch back to the owner still costs something.
sentences.zh: 批量跨线程释放比每次释放一个原子要快，但将批次发送回所有者仍然需要一些费用。

sentences.en: Better to avoid sending it at all when you can.
sentences.zh: 最好尽可能避免发送。

sentences.en: Each thread keeps a small cache of recently freed blocks, one per size class.
sentences.zh: 每个线程都保留一个最近释放的块的小型缓存，每个大小类别一个。

sentences.en: When a thread frees a block that belongs to another thread, it goes into the local cache.
sentences.zh: 当一个线程释放属于另一个线程的块时，它会进入本地缓存。

sentences.en: If the thread later needs a block of that size, it reuses the cached one directly — no cross-thread coordination, no batch to send.
sentences.zh: 如果线程稍后需要该大小的块，它将直接重用缓存的块 - 无需跨线程协调，无需发送批次。

sentences.en: The block only gets routed back to its owner when the cache overflows, the thread goes idle, or the thread exits.
sentences.zh: 仅当缓存溢出、线程空闲或线程退出时，该块才会被路由回其所有者。

blocks.html_en: Each size class gets a cache depth: the byte budget (256 KiB) divided by the class size or the profile’s floor count, whichever is larger, capped at 512 blocks. Large classes need the floor — without it, the byte budget divides down to zero or one entry, and every churn cycle pays a full slab reserve and release.

sentences.en: Each size class gets a cache depth: the byte budget (256 KiB) divided by the class size or the profile’s floor count, whichever is larger, capped at 512 blocks.
sentences.zh: 每个大小类别都有一个缓存深度：字节预算 (256 KiB) 除以类别大小或配置文件的楼层计数（以较大者为准），上限为 512 个块。

sentences.en: Large classes need the floor — without it, the byte budget divides down to zero or one entry, and every churn cycle pays a full slab reserve and release.
sentences.zh: 大型类需要底线 - 没有它，字节预算将分为零或一个条目，并且每个搅动周期都会支付完整的slab 保留和释放。

blocks.html_en: The idle return flushes the entire cache, so the floor costs resident memory only while a thread actively churns. Once a thread parks, its cache is empty.

sentences.en: The idle return flushes the entire cache, so the floor costs resident memory only while a thread actively churns.
sentences.zh: 空闲返回会刷新整个缓存，因此仅当线程主动搅动时才会消耗常驻内存。

sentences.en: Once a thread parks, its cache is empty.
sentences.zh: 一旦线程停顿，其缓存就为空。

blocks.html_en: Memory return¶

sentences.en: Memory return¶
sentences.zh: 内存返回¶

blocks.html_en: When a thread has been idle long enough, it starts giving memory back to the OS. The old allocator never did this. A thread that goes briefly idle and gets work again keeps its memory. But a thread that stays idle gives back everything it holds. Cache, dirty pages, all of it. A parked thread holds nothing.

sentences.en: When a thread has been idle long enough, it starts giving memory back to the OS.
sentences.zh: 当线程空闲足够长的时间时，它开始将内存返还给操作系统。

sentences.en: The old allocator never did this.
sentences.zh: 旧的分配器从未这样做过。

sentences.en: A thread that goes briefly idle and gets work again keeps its memory.
sentences.zh: 短暂空闲并再次开始工作的线程会保留其内存。

sentences.en: But a thread that stays idle gives back everything it holds.
sentences.zh: 但是保持空闲的线程会返回它所持有的所有内容。

sentences.en: Cache, dirty pages, all of it.
sentences.zh: 缓存、脏页，所有这些。

sentences.en: A parked thread holds nothing.
sentences.zh: 停放的线程没有任何内容。

blocks.html_en: The mechanism is a timed tick. An idle thread checks in every 10 milliseconds, doubling the interval each quiet visit up to a 500-millisecond cap. Once it reaches the cap, all held memory goes back to the OS.

sentences.en: The mechanism is a timed tick.
sentences.zh: 该机制是定时滴答。

sentences.en: An idle thread checks in every 10 milliseconds, doubling the interval each quiet visit up to a 500-millisecond cap.
sentences.zh: 空闲线程每 10 毫秒检查一次，将每次安静访问的时间间隔加倍，最多达到 500 毫秒的上限。

sentences.en: Once it reaches the cap, all held memory goes back to the OS.
sentences.zh: 一旦达到上限，所有保留的内存都会返回操作系统。

blocks.html_en: While a thread is active, small freed slabs stay resident and get returned in batches rather than one at a time. Larger freed slabs get returned immediately.

sentences.en: While a thread is active, small freed slabs stay resident and get returned in batches rather than one at a time.
sentences.zh: 当线程处于活动状态时，小的已释放的平板会保持驻留并分批返回，而不是一次返回一个。

sentences.en: Larger freed slabs get returned immediately.
sentences.zh: 较大的释放板会立即返回。

blocks.html_en: I started this post talking about the old allocator hanging on to memory in problematic ways, so what does it look like now? Here are some numbers from testing: 105 MiB of size-class memory, thread goes idle, resident memory falls to 6.5 MiB. The old allocator held all of it, 104 MiB. At a 1 GiB working set, the arena peaks at 1,025 MiB and settles to 27 MiB after idle. The old allocator: 1,019 MiB, start to finish.

sentences.en: I started this post talking about the old allocator hanging on to memory in problematic ways, so what does it look like now?
sentences.zh: 我在这篇文章的开头讨论了旧的分配器以有问题的方式挂在内存上，那么它现在是什么样子的呢？

sentences.en: Here are some numbers from testing: 105 MiB of size-class memory, thread goes idle, resident memory falls to 6.5 MiB.
sentences.zh: 以下是测试中的一些数字：大小级内存为 105 MiB，线程空闲，驻留内存降至 6.5 MiB。

sentences.en: The old allocator held all of it, 104 MiB.
sentences.zh: 旧的分配器保留了所有这些，104 MiB。

sentences.en: At a 1 GiB working set, the arena peaks at 1,025 MiB and settles to 27 MiB after idle.
sentences.zh: 在 1 GiB 工作集下，arena 的峰值为 1,025 MiB，闲置后稳定至 27 MiB。

sentences.en: The old allocator: 1,019 MiB, start to finish.
sentences.zh: 旧分配器：1,019 MiB，从头到尾。

blocks.html_en: The tuning knob¶

sentences.en: The tuning knob¶
sentences.zh: 调音旋钮¶

blocks.html_en: Not every program has the same needs. I spent several days testing different tunable parameters that let you trade memory usage for performance. They’re exposed in a new flag, --ponymemoryprofile, a scale from 1 to 10. The default is 3. At 1, the allocator returns memory to the OS as aggressively as possible — lowest footprint. At 10, it holds on to memory longer to avoid the cost of returning and re-acquiring it — highest throughput.

sentences.en: Not every program has the same needs.
sentences.zh: 并非每个程序都有相同的需求。

sentences.en: I spent several days testing different tunable parameters that let you trade memory usage for performance.
sentences.zh: 我花了几天时间测试不同的可调参数，这些参数可以让您以内存使用换取性能。

sentences.en: They’re exposed in a new flag, --ponymemoryprofile, a scale from 1 to 10.
sentences.zh: 它们暴露在一个新标志 --ponymemoryprofile 中，范围从 1 到 10。

sentences.en: The default is 3.
sentences.zh: 默认值为 3。

sentences.en: At 1, the allocator returns memory to the OS as aggressively as possible — lowest footprint.
sentences.zh: 为 1 时，分配器尽可能积极地将内存返回给操作系统——占用空间最小。

sentences.en: At 10, it holds on to memory longer to avoid the cost of returning and re-acquiring it — highest throughput.
sentences.zh: 在 10 时，它会保留更长时间的内存，以避免返回和重新获取内存的成本 - 最高吞吐量。

blocks.html_en: Every setting returns everything when a thread goes idle. The tradeoff only matters while a thread is actively working.

sentences.en: Every setting returns everything when a thread goes idle.
sentences.zh: 当线程空闲时，每个设置都会返回所有内容。

sentences.en: The tradeoff only matters while a thread is actively working.
sentences.zh: 仅当线程正在积极工作时，这种权衡才重要。

blocks.html_en: What’s next¶

sentences.en: What’s next¶
sentences.zh: 接下来是什么¶

blocks.html_en: The arena allocator is merged to main and is the default on every platform Pony supports. There’s one tradeoff worth knowing: the old allocator was faster in workloads where the working set exceeds the thread cache, because it never gave memory back. That’s the price of reclaiming.

sentences.en: The arena allocator is merged to main and is the default on every platform Pony supports.
sentences.zh: arena 分配器合并到 main 中，并且是 Pony 支持的每个平台上的默认分配器。

sentences.en: There’s one tradeoff worth knowing: the old allocator was faster in workloads where the working set exceeds the thread cache, because it never gave memory back.
sentences.zh: 有一个值得了解的权衡：旧的分配器在工作集超出线程缓存的工作负载中速度更快，因为它永远不会返还内存。

sentences.en: That’s the price of reclaiming.
sentences.zh: 这就是回收的代价。

blocks.html_en: I’m letting the stress tests run for several days to see if they shake out any bugs. Expect a release by the end of the month.

sentences.en: I’m letting the stress tests run for several days to see if they shake out any bugs.
sentences.zh: 我会让压力测试运行几天，看看它们是否消除了任何错误。

sentences.en: Expect a release by the end of the month.
sentences.zh: 预计月底发布。

content_html_zh:
事情是这样的。 很长一段时间以来，我们每天都对 ponyc 的 TCP 系统进行压力测试。 这些测试并没有永远失败。 您可以通过两种方式来看待“没有测试失败”。 要么你的系统坚如磐石，要么你的测试没有覆盖足够的代码库。 我长期以来一直认为压力测试很少失败是因为“测试不够好”。

几个月前，我为此做了一些事情。 我进行了 TCP 压力测试，每次运行都做同样的事情，并添加了一些“群体测试优点”——在每次运行中随机化它们正在做什么以及如何运行。 更多的代码得到了运用，并出现了一堆错误。

这篇文章是关于其中一个“错误”的。

在某些使用模式下，内存会无限增长。 经过一番调查发现，这并不是 TCP 代码本身的错误。 该测试在 Pony 运行时的分配器中触发了一组有趣的边缘情况。

旧分配器可能会以某种方式保留内存，从而导致我在失败的压力测试实例中看到的退化情况，原因有三个。

  1. 在 Pony 中，消息由发送者分配并由接收者释放。 大约一半的释放位于与进行分配的线程不同的线程上。 在错误线程上释放的大块仍然保留，从未回收。 在线程之间传递块的工作负载为其分配和释放的每个块保留新的地址空间，不受限制。 在一万块时，它仍在攀升，每个块大约有 4.3 MiB 地址空间。
  2. 一旦内存被划分为 32 字节槽，它就永远保存 32 字节对象。 分配器从未将其返回为不同的大小。
  3. 两个相邻的空闲块从未合并。 旧的分配器保留了一个排序的空闲列表，混合大小的工作负载在其上的运行速度慢得像爬行一样。 分配 4,000 个块需要 0.49 秒。 16,000 处 39.6 秒。 64,000 个区块在九分钟内还没有完成。

这三个都来自同一个地方：旧的分配器使用一个全局池，其中每个大小类的空闲列表由每个线程共享。 没有线程跟踪它分配了哪些内存。

解决这三个问题的方法是：让每个线程跟踪它分配的内存——什么在使用，什么是空闲的，什么时候区域是空的。 这种跟踪是旧分配器所缺乏的。 有了它，分配器可以合并释放的内存，将空区域返回给操作系统，并跨线程重用内存。

新的分配器¶

受到 snmalloc 基于区域的设计的启发，我构建了一个新的分配器。 内存分为两层：操作系统请求的大区域，分为更小的区域。 每个竞技场属于一个线程。 该线程负责其领域中的所有簿记工作 - 跟踪已分配的内容、空闲的内容以及内存何时可以返回操作系统。 跨线程释放被批量并路由到所属线程，而不是全局处理。

地区和竞技场¶

分配器以称为区域的大对齐块从操作系统请求内存 - 64 位计算机上为 256 MiB，32 位计算机上为 64 MiB。 区域由每个线程共享，并且永远不会取消映射。 通过不取消映射区域，遍历区域列表的线程具有其余设计所依赖的内存安全保证。

线程从区域获取竞技场。 一个 arena 在 64 位上为 8 MiB，在 32 位上为 2 MiB，并且每个都绑定到一个线程。 拥有线程负责维护竞技场的簿记。 当竞技场清空时，其物理页面将返回操作系统，但其地址空间仍保留在该区域中以供重用。

释放内存首先要找到它属于哪个区域。 竞技场的起始地址与其自身的大小对齐。 在 64 位上，每个 arena 都从 8 MiB 边界开始。 屏蔽任何指针的低位，您就可以获得竞技场的基地址。 一条指令。 没有读取内存。 又好又快。 我们喜欢 Ponyland 的这里又好又快。

单位、板和位图¶

一个竞技场分为 16 KiB 单元。 一块板是服务于一种尺寸等级的一个或多个连续单元。 有 16 个大小类别，从 32 字节到 1 MiB，每个类别都是 2 的幂。 对于小类，多个对象适合一个单元 - 32 字节的类每个单元适合 512 个对象。 大班跨越多个单元。

空闲或已用是位图中每个单元一位。 8 MiB 的 arena 有 512 个单元，适合 64 位机器上的 8 个位图字。

内存中彼此相邻的两个空闲单元是位图中彼此相邻的两个零位。 它们已经是一个连续的跨度；没有什么可以合并的。 寻找N个空闲单元就是扫描N个连续的零。 没有合并代码。 没有排序的空闲列表。 没有 O(n) 步行。 旧分配器的块边界（两个相邻的空闲块从未合并）在这里不可能发生，因为表示不允许。 内存中的邻接是位图中的邻接，位图中的邻接是跨度。 一直都是。

在一个方向上提升首次适应会在另一个方向上留下长跑。 如果没有这种分割，单个单元分配将会分割多单元板所需的大跨度。

竞技场簿记——位图、每单位记录——存在于竞技场的开始阶段。 分配的对象前面没有任何东西。

跨线程释放¶

在 Pony 中，消息由运行发送者的线程分配，并由运行接收者的线程释放。 这些通常是不同的线程。 跨线程释放并不是一种边缘情况——它们不断发生，并且分配器必须快速处理它们。

直接的方法是每个外部释放一个原子操作：将释放的对象推送到所属线程的收件箱中。 然而，测试表明，在争用情况下，性能崩溃了。 直接的方法行不通。

相反，释放线程收集释放的对象并将它们批量发送给所有者。 一个原子可进行 32 次释放，而不是 32 个原子可进行 32 次释放。 批处理和非批处理之间的性能差异是巨大的。 拥有线程处理释放的内存并可以重用它。

线程缓存¶

批量跨线程释放比每次释放一个原子要快，但将批次发送回所有者仍然需要一些费用。 最好尽可能避免发送。 每个线程都保留一个最近释放的块的小型缓存，每个大小类别一个。 当一个线程释放属于另一个线程的块时，它会进入本地缓存。 如果线程稍后需要该大小的块，它将直接重用缓存的块 - 无需跨线程协调，无需发送批次。 仅当缓存溢出、线程空闲或线程退出时，该块才会被路由回其所有者。

每个大小类别都有一个缓存深度：字节预算 (256 KiB) 除以类别大小或配置文件的楼层计数（以较大者为准），上限为 512 个块。 大型类需要底线 - 没有它，字节预算将分为零或一个条目，并且每个搅动周期都会支付完整的slab 保留和释放。

空闲返回会刷新整个缓存，因此仅当线程主动搅动时才会消耗常驻内存。 一旦线程停顿，其缓存就为空。

内存返回¶

当线程空闲足够长的时间时，它开始将内存返还给操作系统。 旧的分配器从未这样做过。 短暂空闲并再次开始工作的线程会保留其内存。 但是保持空闲的线程会返回它所持有的所有内容。 缓存、脏页，所有这些。 停放的线程没有任何内容。

该机制是定时滴答。 空闲线程每 10 毫秒检查一次，将每次安静访问的时间间隔加倍，最多达到 500 毫秒的上限。 一旦达到上限，所有保留的内存都会返回操作系统。

当线程处于活动状态时，小的已释放的平板会保持驻留并分批返回，而不是一次返回一个。 较大的释放板会立即返回。

我在这篇文章的开头讨论了旧的分配器以有问题的方式挂在内存上，那么它现在是什么样子的呢？ 以下是测试中的一些数字：大小级内存为 105 MiB，线程空闲，驻留内存降至 6.5 MiB。 旧的分配器保留了所有这些，104 MiB。 在 1 GiB 工作集下，arena 的峰值为 1,025 MiB，闲置后稳定至 27 MiB。 旧分配器：1,019 MiB，从头到尾。

调音旋钮¶

并非每个程序都有相同的需求。 我花了几天时间测试不同的可调参数，这些参数可以让您以内存使用换取性能。 它们暴露在一个新标志 --ponymemoryprofile 中，范围从 1 到 10。 默认值为 3。 为 1 时，分配器尽可能积极地将内存返回给操作系统——占用空间最小。 在 10 时，它会保留更长时间的内存，以避免返回和重新获取内存的成本 - 最高吞吐量。

当线程空闲时，每个设置都会返回所有内容。 仅当线程正在积极工作时，这种权衡才重要。

接下来是什么¶

arena 分配器合并到 main 中，并且是 Pony 支持的每个平台上的默认分配器。 有一个值得了解的权衡：旧的分配器在工作集超出线程缓存的工作负载中速度更快，因为它永远不会返还内存。 这就是回收的代价。
